--- title: "[Family]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-abc}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Abstract family defining the response distribution and link function. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/base.py#L10-L166){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python Family() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A `Family` encapsulates everything the P-IRLS fitting loop needs to know about the conditional distribution of the response `y` given the linear predictor `eta`. Every GLM and GAM family in Whittaker belongs to the exponential dispersion family, and is fully characterized by three ingredients: 1. The **link function** `g`, relating the mean `mu` to the linear predictor `eta`: `eta = g(mu)`, along with its inverse and derivative. 2. The **variance function** `V(mu)`, relating the variance of the response to its mean: `Var(Y) = phi * V(mu)`, where `phi` is the dispersion (scale) parameter. 3. The **deviance** and **log-likelihood**, which quantify goodness of fit and are used by `GAM.fit()` for smoothing parameter selection (GCV/REML) and by `GAM.summary()` for reporting. Subclasses must implement all abstract methods (`link`, `link_inverse`, `link_derivative`, `variance`, `deviance`, `log_likelihood`, `simulate`). The link function and its inverse/derivative are used by the P-IRLS algorithm to form pseudo-data (the working response `z`) and working weights `W` at each iteration. Families whose loss does not fit the standard GLM deviance framework (e.g. `QuantileFamily`, `CoxPH`, `OrderedCategorical`, `Multinomial`) may instead override `irls_update` to supply `z` and `W` directly. Whittaker ships with the following concrete families: - `Gaussian` — identity link, constant variance; the default family for continuous, unbounded responses. - `Poisson` — log link, `V(mu) = mu`; for count data. - `Binomial` — logit link, `V(mu) = mu(1-mu)`; for binary or proportion responses. - `Gamma` — log link, `V(mu) = mu^2`; for positive, right-skewed continuous data. - `NegativeBinomial` — log link, `V(mu) = mu + mu^2/theta`; for overdispersed counts. - `Beta` — logit link; for proportions strictly between 0 and 1. - `Tweedie` / `TweedieEstimated` (via `tw()`) — log link, `V(mu) = mu^p`; for compound Poisson-Gamma data with a point mass at zero (e.g. insurance claims). - `InverseGaussian` — log link, `V(mu) = mu^3`; for positive, heavy-tailed continuous data. - `CoxPH` — proportional hazards partial likelihood; for survival/time-to-event data. - `OrderedCategorical` — cumulative logit (proportional odds); for ordinal responses. - `Multinomial` — baseline-category logit; for unordered categorical responses. - `QuantileFamily` — Extended Log-F (ELF) smooth pinball loss; for quantile regression. For distributional regression, where more than one parameter of the response distribution (e.g. both the mean and the scale) is modeled by its own smooth predictor, see `GAMLSSFamily` and its concrete subclasses (`GaussianLS`, `GammaLS`, `BetaLS`, `ZeroInflatedPoisson`, `ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomial`). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Families are passed to `GAM` via the `family` argument; they are rarely instantiated by users beyond that. ::: {#f0d94935 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 200 x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) y = rng.poisson(np.exp(0.5 * np.sin(x))) data = {"x": x, "y": y} # Any concrete Family subclass can be passed to GAM model = wk.GAM("y ~ s(x)", family=wk.Poisson()) model.fit(data, method="REML") print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAM fit summary ============================================================ Formula: y ~ s(x) Family: Poisson(link='log') Observations: 200 Coefficients: 10 Parametric coefficients: Term Estimate Std.Err z value p-value ------------------------ ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- (Intercept) 0.2113 0.0657 3.214 0.00131 Approximate significance of smooth terms: Term EDF Ref.df Chi.sq p-value ------------------------ ------ ------ ---------- ---------- s(x) 4.18 5 37.260 5.312e-07 Total EDF: 5.18 Deviance: 187.0851 Null dev: 230.5815 Dev. expl: 18.9% GCV score: 0.985797 Scale est: 1.000000 AIC: 554.30 BIC: 571.37 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
scale_known Whether the scale parameter is fixed (True for Binomial, Poisson).
### [scale_known]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Whether the scale parameter is fixed (True for Binomial, Poisson). ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [scale_known]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
deviance() Total (unscaled) deviance: 2 * Σ [ℓ(y; y) − ℓ(y; μ)].
initialize() Starting values for μ given the response *y*.
irls_update() Custom IRLS pseudo-response and working weights.
link() Apply the link function: η = g(μ).
link_derivative() Derivative of the link function: dη/dμ = g'(μ).
link_inverse() Apply the inverse link: μ = g⁻¹(η).
log_likelihood() Log-likelihood ℓ(y; μ, φ) evaluated at the given scale parameter φ.
simulate() Simulate response values from the distribution.
unit_deviance() Per-observation deviance contributions d_i (before summing).
variance() Variance function V(μ).
### [deviance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Total (unscaled) deviance: 2 * Σ [ℓ(y; y) − ℓ(y; μ)]. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/base.py#L101-L107){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python deviance(y, mu, *, weights=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} When *weights* is given the deviance is Σ w_i d_i. ::: ### [initialize()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Starting values for μ given the response *y*. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/base.py#L160-L166){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python initialize(y) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The default returns *y* unchanged, which is appropriate for Gaussian with identity link. Families with non-identity links or constrained means should override this. ::: ### [irls_update()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Custom IRLS pseudo-response and working weights. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/base.py#L151-L158){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python irls_update(y, mu, eta) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Override in families whose loss is not a standard GLM deviance (e.g. quantile regression). Return `(z, W)` where *z* is the pseudo-response and *W* is the diagonal working-weight vector. Return `None` to use the default GLM formula. ::: ### [link()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Apply the link function: η = g(μ). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/base.py#L78-L81){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link(mu) ``` ::: ### [link_derivative()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Derivative of the link function: dη/dμ = g'(μ). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/base.py#L88-L91){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_derivative(mu) ``` ::: ### [link_inverse()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Apply the inverse link: μ = g⁻¹(η). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/base.py#L83-L86){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_inverse(eta) ``` ::: ### [log_likelihood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Log-likelihood ℓ(y; μ, φ) evaluated at the given scale parameter φ. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/base.py#L116-L124){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python log_likelihood(y, mu, scale, *, weights=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} When *weights* is given the log-likelihood is Σ w_i ℓ_i. ::: ### [simulate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Simulate response values from the distribution. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/base.py#L131-L149){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python simulate(mu, scale, rng) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Mean (fitted values), shape `(n,)`. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Estimated scale parameter φ. [rng]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [object]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A `numpy.random.Generator` instance. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Simulated response values, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [unit_deviance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Per-observation deviance contributions d_i (before summing). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/base.py#L109-L114){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python unit_deviance(y, mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Default implementation: `(y - mu)^2` (Gaussian). Override for other families. ::: ### [variance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Variance function V(μ). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/base.py#L93-L99){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python variance(mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For the Gaussian family this is constant (1); for Poisson it is μ, etc. :::
